genre: narrated brand manifesto sizzle with burned-in captions
why_this_genre: Cue was a product ad and ORRIN was a product film. The Aurus reference is neither: a narrated manifesto that never shows a product, cuts a montage of unrelated worlds against a spoken argument, and resolves on a logo. It is the only genre in the inspected library that is carried by voice and rhythm rather than by an object.
craft_targets: Pacing: a deliberate rhythm change. Act one cuts at 1.2-1.8s, act two slows to 3-4s, act three holds. Both previous films ran one flat 4-6s cadence.
Transitions: designed handoffs instead of hard cuts only - whip pans on matched screen direction in act one, a dip through black into water, warm dissolves in act three.
Coverage: buy roughly 60 seconds of footage for a 38-second film so weak shots can simply be dropped. Both previous films bought exactly what they needed and had to use it.
Colour arc: cold cyan -> deep teal -> warm amber, so the argument's turn is visible before it is heard.
design_rules: No dialogue in any plate; the narration is a separate local TTS track.
Every legible glyph is authored in HyperFrames.
Act one shots all move left-to-right so whip-pan handoffs are motivated.
Routing follows the measured loops: Veo 3.1 Fast with audio off for environment and landscape, Kling 3.0 Pro for faceless hands.
